subject: computer-science
title: Databases: Foundations
welcome_lead: Tables, rows and columns — meet the world of organised data.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on database foundations: tables, records and primary keys.
final_note: You now know how databases are structured and why keys matter.

concepts.def: An organised, persistent store of data.
Rows are records; columns are fields.
A field that uniquely identifies each record.
Language to query and manage a relational database.
A request to select or change data.

walkthroughs.body_html: Imagine a Students table. Each row = one student (a record). Each column = one fact about them (a field), e.g. StudentID, Name, Year.
Two students might share the name 'Alex Smith'. A primary key like StudentID 1234 is unique, so we never confuse records.
A single big table works for tiny data, but quickly causes duplication (same teacher's name on every row) and update errors when something changes.

mcqs.q: Which field would make the best primary key for a customer table?
options: A unique CustomerID number
The customer's surname
The customer's town
The customer's favourite colour

mcqs.q: A field in a database table is:
options: One column holding a single category of data
One complete row of data
A backup copy of the table
The name of the database file
Find and filter records that match chosen criteria
Physically repair the disk
Print the database manual
Slow down data entry

mcqs.q: Compared with a flat-file database, a relational database:
options: Stores data in multiple linked tables, reducing duplicated data
Stores everything in one giant table
Cannot use primary keys
Holds only numbers

mcqs.q: Is the primary key always the first column of a table?
options: Yes - whatever column comes first automatically becomes the key.
No - the primary key is defined by its uniqueness property, not its position; it can be any field that uniquely identifies each record.
Yes - relational databases are only used for very small data.
Yes - tables refuse to save unless the key is in column one.

mcqs.q: Are a record and a field the same thing?
options: Yes - tables refuse to save unless the key is in column one.
A record is a column and a field is a row.
No - a record is one row (everything about one item), while a field is one column (one category of data across all items).
Yes - record and field both mean a box in the table.

mcqs.q: Would using one big table for customers and their orders be simpler and better?
options: Yes - one table is always simpler, so it is always better.
Yes - relational databases are only used for very small data.
Yes - tables refuse to save unless the key is in column one.
No - repeating customer details on every order duplicates data, wasting space and causing inconsistencies; linked tables store each fact once.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Primary key”?
options: A field whose value is unique for every record, used to identify each record unambiguously, like a customer ID.
A single column of a table, holding one category of data, such as Surname or DateOfBirth, with a set data type.
A grid of rows and columns holding data about one type of thing, such as all of a school's students.
A single row of a table, containing all the stored data about one individual item or person.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Query”?
options: A grid of rows and columns holding data about one type of thing, such as all of a school's students.
A field whose value is unique for every record, used to identify each record unambiguously, like a customer ID.
A single row of a table, containing all the stored data about one individual item or person.
A request to a database to find, filter or sort data matching chosen criteria, returning just the records required.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Field”?
options: A single column of a table, holding one category of data, such as Surname or DateOfBirth, with a set data type.
A field whose value is unique for every record, used to identify each record unambiguously, like a customer ID.
A grid of rows and columns holding data about one type of thing, such as all of a school's students.
A request to a database to find, filter or sort data matching chosen criteria, returning just the records required.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Table”?
options: A grid of rows and columns holding data about one type of thing, such as all of a school's students.
A field whose value is unique for every record, used to identify each record unambiguously, like a customer ID.
A single column of a table, holding one category of data, such as Surname or DateOfBirth, with a set data type.
An organised, persistent collection of related data, structured so information can be stored, searched and updated efficiently.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Database”?
options: A single row of a table, containing all the stored data about one individual item or person.
A request to a database to find, filter or sort data matching chosen criteria, returning just the records required.
A single column of a table, holding one category of data, such as Surname or DateOfBirth, with a set data type.
An organised, persistent collection of related data, structured so information can be stored, searched and updated efficiently.

options: A single row of a table, containing all the stored data about one individual item or person.
An organised, persistent collection of related data, structured so information can be stored, searched and updated efficiently.
A request to a database to find, filter or sort data matching chosen criteria, returning just the records required.

150 values
31 values
